questions.prompt: Put these kinds of mods in order from smallest change to largest change.
questions.explanation: Reskins change only looks, config tweaks change exposed values, asset additions add new content, and a total conversion replaces nearly everything.

questions.prompt: Buying a game gives a player a license to play it, not ownership of its code, art, and music.
questions.explanation: The studio keeps the copyright, and the EULA sets the terms of the license.

questions.prompt: Which of these are generally considered acceptable modding practice?
choices: Using a developer-provided modding SDK as intended
Making a personal, non-commercial mod that requires owning the base game
Bundling the game's original copyrighted assets in a standalone download
Redistributing licensed music from the game as part of a mod
answers: Using a developer-provided modding SDK as intended
Making a personal, non-commercial mod that requires owning the base game
questions.explanation: SDK use and base-game-dependent personal mods are usually tolerated; redistributing the studio's copyrighted assets is what crosses the line.

questions.prompt: Why do most games bundle their assets into large archive files such as .pak or .vpk?
choices: Faster loading and light tamper-resistance, but not real encryption
To strongly encrypt the assets so they cannot be read
Because textures cannot be stored as separate files
To make mods legally impossible
questions.answer: Faster loading and light tamper-resistance, but not real encryption
questions.explanation: Reading one large file is faster than opening thousands of small ones, and a custom container gives only light obfuscation.

questions.prompt: Match each file format to the kind of file it is.
questions.explanation: DDS is a GPU-friendly texture format, FBX bundles meshes, OGG holds audio, and INI files are human-readable settings.

questions.prompt: A game reads a weapon's damage from a config file instead of hard-coding it. What is this design approach called?
questions.explanation: Data-driven design lets designers and modders change numbers without recompiling the game.

questions.prompt: A sandbox lets a mod script call only the functions the game's API exposes, and blocks things like reading arbitrary files or making network requests.
questions.explanation: Sandboxing restricts scripts to the functions the API deliberately provides.

questions.prompt: Which of these does a modding framework typically provide?
choices: A mod loader that finds and loads installed mods in order
A shared API layer richer than the base game's
A way for mods to declare dependencies on other mods
A decompiler that rebuilds the game's original source code
Automatic ownership of the game's assets
answers: A mod loader that finds and loads installed mods in order
A shared API layer richer than the base game's
A way for mods to declare dependencies on other mods
questions.explanation: Frameworks handle loading, shared functionality, and dependency and conflict management.

questions.prompt: Explain what an event hook is and why load order matters when several mods hook the same event.
rubric: Says the game announces or fires a named event when something happens
Says registered scripts (callbacks) run automatically in response
Says this works without changing the game's original logic
Says several mods can hook the same event and the order decides which changes win or conflict
questions.model: An event hook is a named point where the game announces that something happened, such as an item pickup, and any script registered as a callback runs in response without editing the original game logic. Several unrelated mods can hook the same event, so the order they run in decides whose changes win or whether they conflict.
questions.explanation: Hooks let mods react to events; order matters because callbacks and mods can overwrite each other.

questions.prompt: A sword deals 12 damage per hit and attacks 1.5 times per second. What is its damage per second (DPS)?
questions.explanation: DPS is damage times attacks per second: 12 x 1.5 = 18.

questions.prompt: What does UV mapping describe in a model swap?
choices: How points on the 3D surface correspond to points on the flat texture image
The volume of audio attached to a model
The version number of the model file
How many bones a rig contains
questions.answer: How points on the 3D surface correspond to points on the flat texture image
questions.explanation: A replacement texture must match the model's UV layout or it will look stretched or misplaced.

questions.prompt: What is the name for a small third mod built to reconcile two other mods' conflicting changes?
questions.explanation: A compatibility patch fixes the conflict so neither original author has to.

questions.prompt: How does a memory scanner help find the value that stores a player's health?
choices: It looks for a value that changes in step with an action, such as taking exactly 10 damage
It rebuilds the original source code
It reads the developer's design documents
It decrypts the game's archives
questions.answer: It looks for a value that changes in step with an action, such as taking exactly 10 damage
questions.explanation: A memory scanner finds correlation between your actions and changing values; it does not recover source code.

questions.prompt: A mod you installed crashes the game, and the game has no official modding support. Describe how you would diagnose it.
rubric: Checks the game's log file or crash dump
Reads the error message for the likely cause
Changes one thing at a time and retests
Consults community wikis, forums, or Discord
questions.model: I would open the game's log or crash dump and read the error to see what failed. Then I would change or disable one thing at a time and retest to isolate the cause, and I would check the community wiki or forums to see if others hit the same problem.
questions.explanation: Most modding problems are solved with logs, one-change-at-a-time tests, and community knowledge before any advanced tools.

questions.prompt: Under DMCA Section 1201, circumventing a technical protection measure can be illegal even if the resulting use would otherwise be fair use.
questions.explanation: Section 1201 targets the act of circumvention itself, independent of whether the underlying use would be allowed.

questions.prompt: Match each part of a semantic version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) to when it is incremented.
pairs: A new feature that does not break existing users
questions.explanation: Semantic versioning gives dependency declarations a reliable signal about how risky an update is.

questions.prompt: Which items belong in a clean mod package?
choices: Only the files you changed
A manifest with the name, author, version, and dependencies
A readme with install steps and requirements
A copy of the game's original archives
answers: A manifest with the name, author, version, and dependencies
A readme with install steps and requirements
questions.explanation: Package only your changes with a manifest and readme; never include the original game's files.

questions.prompt: Why should a mod be tested alongside several popular mods and not only on its own?
choices: Real players run many mods, and conflicts like overwriting the same value only appear when mods are combined
Testing alone is not allowed by most EULAs
A mod that works alone is always safe with others
Popular mods always fix conflicts automatically
questions.answer: Real players run many mods, and conflicts like overwriting the same value only appear when mods are combined
questions.explanation: Mod conflicts occur when independent mods change the same element, which isolated testing cannot reveal.
